To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we augment the LibriSpeech corpus with synthetic speech to train end-to-end neural ASR systems, and we achieve state of the arts WERs for character-level models without an external LM.

(1) augmenting a natural speech dataset by adding synthetic speech can improve the performance of a neural speech recognition model; (2) the improvement in performance is dependent on the quality of the synthetic speech and (3) the performance of a character-level based neural speech recognition model can be improved by using synthetic speech augmentation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following two questions: (1) How can we augment natural speech datasets using synthetic speech and (2) How can we train large neural models using these augmented datasets?

the use of synthetic data for ASR training is a promising approach for building accurate models, especially for languages where large datasets are not available.
the use of synthetic speech augmentation is an efficient and effective way to improve speech recognition performance.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that augmenting a natural speech dataset using synthetic speech is a viable approach to improve the performance of ASR models.
we are able to achieve state of the arts WER for character-level based neural ASR models without an external LM.

(i) we propose a novel approach to augment a natural ASR dataset with synthetic data, (ii) we train very large end to end neural ASR models using the augmented data, and (iii) we achieve state of the-art WER for character-level based ASR systems without an external language models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
synthetic data can be used to train very large models that achieve state of theart WER on the LibriSpeech test set.
